articles.title: 马斯克：第二代 Roadster 将是最后一款“人工驾驶”特斯拉车型
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，特斯拉将未来押注于自动驾驶，第二代 Roadster 是一个重要例外。特斯拉 CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克在发布会上宣布，随着 Model S 和 Model X 即将退出产品阵容，Roadster 最终将成为特斯拉唯一一款专为人工驾驶打造的车型。“从长远来看，这台车实际上将是特斯拉最后一款由人亲自驾驶的汽车…… 既然只有这么一款，那就要把它的性能推向极限，甚至突破极限。”特斯拉希望将 Roadster 打造成旗下的性能旗舰。新车采用了多项技术，能够在加速、过弯和综合性能方面达到惊人水平。其中一项是车底的风扇吸附系统，旨在让车辆过弯时额外获得最高 2g 的横向加速度。该系统借鉴了 SpaceX 的技术研发成果，将特斯拉在航空航天领域的部分技术理念应用于汽车。特斯拉还宣称，Roadster 的 0 至 97km/h 加速时间不到 1 秒。据IT之家了解，新车计划于 2028 年投产。相关阅读：《特斯拉能飞：第二代 Roadster 预订意向金 33.2 万元起，马斯克宣布 2028 年量产》《这次能飞了！特斯拉第二代 Roadster 跑车正式亮相》

articles.title: 阿里云虚拟数字人启动退市：11 月 30 日停止新购服务，明年 11 月底全面停止
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，阿里云今日宣布，由于产品策略调整，虚拟数字人产品即将退市。退市的具体安排如下：2026 年 11 月 30 日，停止新购服务，已购买的客户仍可继续使用至服务到期。2027 年 5 月 31 日，停止现有客户的续订及版本更新。2027 年 11 月 30 日，全面停止服务。届时控制台、相关的支持服务和工单服务也将一同下线。此外，阿里云提供的退款服务也将于该日期停止，如果您有退款需求，请在截止日期前尽早联系，安排退款操作。官方表示，为保障业务连续性，建议用户尽快迁移至替换方案：阿里云云市场数字人产品蚂蚁灵境数字人、相芯数字人、一知智能 AI 直播数字人。IT之家查询阿里云官网获悉，虚拟数字人是由通义实验室打造的虚拟数字人平台，提供涵盖形象定制、AI 智能驱动到场景化落地的全链路数字人解决方案。平台致力于通过数字人技术赋能企业数字化转型，并深度服务于智慧教育、新闻媒体等多个行业，全面满足视频播报、业务咨询、互动交流、服务导览等多样化需求，为客户打造高效、智能、一站式数字人服务体验。

articles.title: 丹麦最高法院裁定：AI 生成儿童色情内容同样获刑
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子判处的 18 个月监禁刑罚。该男子因持有并传播数万张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像而获刑。这起备受关注的案件，涉及丹麦现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律如何适用于 AI 合成内容。该国最高法院裁定，即使 AI 生成的未成年人色情图像没有真实人物作为原型，也同样受到丹麦《刑法》约束，不能因为图像中的人物是虚构的就减轻刑罚。此前，两级下级法院对本案的量刑存在分歧。判决指出，对于持有和传播描绘未满 18 岁者的色情材料，在量刑时不应考虑图像中的人物是否被认为是虚构的。据IT之家了解，该男子被判处的 18 个月监禁不适用缓刑。这是丹麦首起因制作和传播 AI 生成的儿童性虐待影像而定罪的案件，最高法院也借此首次明确了此类犯罪在丹麦法律下的量刑原则。涉案男子曾利用 AI 制作超过 3.6 万张逼真的儿童色情图像，并通过网站和聊天频道传播。法庭文件显示，他还通过订阅服务出售部分图像，至少赚取 2.5 万丹麦克朗（IT之家注：现汇率约合 24,801 元人民币）。警方 2023 年底突击搜查其住所时，男子 28 岁。他承认制作和传播图像的行为，但认为这些图像并非以真人为原型，因此不应受到有关刑法条款的处罚。去年，此案还引发了一场跨国警方行动，调查对象包括数百名购买这些图像的人。警方根据支付记录查明 273 人的身份，并在世界各地逮捕 25 人。丹麦两级下级法院均认为，即使图像完全由 AI 合成，只要足够逼真，也可以依据现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律追究刑事责任。但两级法院在具体量刑上存在明显分歧。2025 年 1 月，地方法院判处其 15 个月监禁，但允许大部分刑期缓期执行，理由之一是没有证据表明 AI 模型曾使用真实的儿童性虐待影像进行训练。同年晚些时候，高等法院改判 18 个月实刑，理由是涉案图像数量庞大、传播活动有组织地开展，且部分图像被用于牟利。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，振华 (Super Flower) 现已在电商平台销售 LEADEX VIII PRO 系列电源。其采用 ATX 外形规格，但长度缩短至 125mm；搭配“九宫格”盲插模组接口和纯铜芯镀锡模组线。该系列电源符合 ATX12V 3.1 规范，提供 600W 12V-2×6 输出，通过 Cybenetics 白金转换效率认证。其电解与固态电容均来自日系一线品牌，搭配英飞凌 MOS、专利双层立式微型变压器，可稳定承受 200% 整机瞬态超载，12V 满载纹波低至 21.66mW。此外，LEADEX VIII PRO 内置 120mm 尺寸 FDB 轴承风扇，支持智能启停模式，获得 Cybenetics A-认证；具备 OVP、OCP、OPP、SCP、UVP、OTP、NLO、SIP 八大安全机制，享受 10 年质保。振华 LEADEX VIII PRO 系列电源目前包含 850W / 1000W / 1200W 三个版本，当前售价分别为 1159 元 / 1299 元 / 1499 元。京东振华 LEADEX VIII PRO 电源 1159 元起直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 10 年授权未能跻身主流：诺基亚品牌手机操盘手 HMD 曝收缩全球战线
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，消息源 @smashx_60 于 10 月 14 日在 X 平台发布推文，爆料称 HMD Global 正酝酿战略收缩，逐步退出部分市场，并全面减产硬件产品线。消息称在本次战略调整后，HMD 将会聚焦特定区域市场，资源重心向利润空间更高的企业与工业（Enterprise / Industrial）垂直领域倾斜。这意味着，在竞争白热化的消费级全球手机舞台上，我们后续可能很难再看到 HMD 全球旗舰新品发布。IT之家附上相关截图如下：自 2016 年从微软手中接过诺基亚手机品牌长达 10 年的独占授权以来，HMD 曾凭借复刻诺基亚 3310 等情怀神机引发轰动。然而，在苹果与三星等巨头产品热销等的残酷现实下，诺基亚品牌智能手机在消费市场始终未能跻身主流。双方最初于 2016 年签下了为期 10 年的全球独家授权协议。但在 2023 年 8 月的补充协议中，双方明确将智能手机与平板的排他性授权截止日锁定在 2026 年 3 月。HMD 已不再生产新款诺基亚智能手机，全面转向自有品牌“HMD”。由于诺基亚品牌的功能机（如 3310、105 等复刻版）在印度、中东及非洲等新兴市场依然极具号召力和庞大的市场份额，双方在原有 2026 年到期的基础上，消息称签署了续约协议，将功能机授权延长了约 3 年至 2029 年。

articles.title: 苹果官网线上 Apple Store 开始维护，首款折叠屏 iPhone Duo 今晚 8 点预购
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 今晚 8 点开启预购，目前苹果官网线上 Apple Store 商店已开始维护。综合IT之家此前报道，苹果在 2026 年秋季发布会上发布了 iPhone Duo，于 10 月 16 日晚 8 点接受预购，10 月 23 日正式发售，定价 15,999 元起。256GB：15,999 元512GB：17,999 元1TB：21,499 元2TB：26,499 元iPhone Duo 提供星光白和夜空双色可选，手机内外屏均为 120Hz（ProMotion），支持 Apple Pencil（今年晚些时候），其中内屏尺寸为 7.6 英寸（采用屏下摄像头），外屏 5.4 英寸。iPhone Duo 前置 12Mp 自拍摄像头，后置 48Mp 主摄及 48Mp 融合式超广角，支持拍摄 4K 杜比视界 HDR 视频，提供全新“智能拍摄”功能，不需要用户动手按快门即可自动拍摄。iPhone Duo 搭载 A20 Pro 处理器，拥有大尺寸 VC 均热板，手机全球版本均采用 eSIM 设计，匹配 C2 基带芯片，在软硬件加持下，手机充满一次电续航至高 24 小时，使用外屏播放视频提供至高 44 小时续航，手机充电 5 分钟可在外屏上观看 5 小时视频。需要注意的是，iPhone Duo 仅支持 eSIM 卡。京东 iPhone Duo【仅支持 eSIM】15999 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，AI 公司 PrismML 昨日（10 月 15 日）发布博文，宣布推出 Ternary Bonsai 2 系列模型，共有 2B、4B 和 9B 三种规模，目标在手机、PC 以及可穿戴设备上本地运行 AI 智能体，执行推理、识图、调用工具等能力。Ternary Bonsai 2 系列模型基于阿里的 Qwen 3.5 基座构建，采用“三元”权重表示法，即仅用 -1、0、+1 三种数值编码模型参数。官方称，2B、4B、9B 模型的存储占用分别约为 0.43GB、0.95GB 和 2GB。在能力上，Bonsai 2 系列强调本地智能体的实用性：遵循指令、完成日常任务、在移动设备上调用工具、避免重复输出等。官方在 19 项基准上测试了智能工具调用、数学、指令遵循、编程、知识与推理、视觉理解六类能力；其中 9B 模型在标准指令执行和日常数学任务中，所需 token 数量约减少 40%。性能方面，PrismML 表示，在 RTX 4090 和 M5 Pro 等硬件上，新模型相较对应全精度模型可实现最高 5 倍吞吐量和 3 倍能效；在 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上，9B 模型最高可达每秒 34 个词元，2B 模型最高可达每秒 120 个词元。IT之家附上相关截图如下：该系列可与已有的 Bonsai 2 27B 组成从轻量任务到复杂工作流的完整产品线。开发者可通过 llama.cpp 在 NVIDIA GPU 上运行，也可通过 MLX 在 Mac、iPhone 和 iPad 上部署；模型权重以 Apache 2.0 许可证开放。

articles.title: 马斯克回应第二代 Roadster 跑车能否合法上路：能不能要看道路情况
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，汽车媒体 insideevs 今天（10 月 16 日）发布博文，报道称针对车主最关心的第二代 Roadster 跑车能否合法上路，全球首富埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）并未给出明确答案，并解读认为可能仅适用于私人场地以及部分支持地区。IT之家今天报道，在美国得克萨斯州韦科市的 SpaceX 工厂内，特斯拉现场演示了第二代 Roadster 跑车，借助压缩空气推进器腾空跃起、越过一排车辆，并完成空中桶滚。关于第二代 Roadster 跑车合法上路，马斯克先称“这将是一辆真正能上路的汽车”，随后又补充说“我不确定它在所有司法辖区是否合法，但肯定会有人能拥有这样一辆车”。当现场观众追问是否合法上路时，他回应：“取决于你所在的街道。”技术层面，Roadster 配备可产生约 2G 下压力的风扇吸附系统，甚至能倒置行驶；车尾四个 SpaceX 推进器据称可将 0-60 英里 / 小时加速时间压缩至 0.81 秒。马斯克宣称它将“打破所有现有赛道纪录”。特斯拉官网显示，Roadster 将提供三个版本：Performance 版标注“可容纳两人、随时上路”；Thrust 版为“赛道级”，增加加速推进器；而具备飞行能力的 Rocket 版仅限受邀预订，描述为“可容纳一人”。相关阅读：《特斯拉能飞：第二代 Roadster 预订意向金 33.2 万元起，马斯克宣布 2028 年量产》《这次能飞了！特斯拉第二代 Roadster 跑车正式亮相》《特斯拉第二代 Roadster 发布正式定档：北京时间 16 日上午 8:55 见》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，数码博主 @i冰宇宙 今天（10 月 16 日）援引《首尔经济日报》报道，称三星在为 Galaxy S27 Ultra 旗舰手机做最终性能验证时，发现高通第六代骁龙 8 超级至尊版（Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme 6th generation）存在过热问题。报道称内部测试显示，该芯片在高负载运行时温度反复超过阈值，并出现处理速度下降的情况。三星已于上月（2026 年 9 月）将测试结果反馈给高通，并要求其在 10 月中旬前完成改进。IT之家援引博文介绍，双方目前仍在持续优化并重新测试。三星计划在本月中旬评估高通的散热改进进展，并最终确定处理器方案。若问题无法解决，三星可能改用自研的 Exynos 2700。若 Exynos 2700 最终入选，将是 Ultra 系列时隔五年再次搭载 Exynos 芯片。此前，三星在 2022 年的欧洲版 Galaxy S22 Ultra 上使用 Exynos 2200，自 2023 年 Galaxy S23 Ultra 起，Ultra 机型全球统一采用高通处理器。相关阅读：《三星 Galaxy S27 Ultra 手机爆料：AI 减少镜头光晕，充电提速约 3%》《消息称三星电子已量产 Exynos 2700 处理器，Galaxy S27 系列手机将搭载》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据外媒 NotebookCheck 今天（16 日）午间报道，Honeycomb 的飞行模拟手柄 Echo Aviation Controller XPC 现已在美国开放免费预约，售价 179.99 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,206 元人民币），将于 11 月 20 日正式开售，随后陆续登陆其他市场。该手柄兼容 XBOX 和 PC，配备隧道磁阻摇杆、霍尔效应方向舵拨片以及 4 个滑块，专为《微软模拟飞行》打造。用户现可通过 Honeycomb 官网免费预约，暂时不能直接预购。此外，Honeycomb 欧洲商城也已上架 Echo XPC，标价 179.99 欧元（现汇率约合 1,352 元人民币）。Echo XPC 获得了 XBOX 官方授权，也能在 PC 上使用，将 Alpha 飞行驾驶盘、Bravo 油门控制台和 Charlie 方向舵踏板的主要功能整合进一款手柄之中。其采用 16 位隧道磁阻摇杆控制飞机俯仰和横滚，手柄背面的方向舵拨片仍采用霍尔效应传感器，两个拨片通过机械结构联动，并支持自动回中。Echo XPC 还配备 4 个带定位挡位的滑块，可用于控制油门、襟翼和减速板。用户可以更换滑块帽，适配通用航空飞机或民航客机的操纵布局。其他操纵部件包括带防滑纹理的配平滚轮、调整视角的帽形开关，以及分别控制襟翼、起落架和驻机刹车的独立拨杆。手柄支持 USB 有线和无线连接，可通过 USB-C 充电，官方标称续航最长 15 小时。

articles.title: 智元宣布与首批 20+ 高校合作，投入超 2 亿元建设具身智能人才生态
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，智元本周发布公告，“元苼生态发展计划”与国内众多高校开展合作，共建具身智能产教融合创新实践平台。基于具身智能真实教学与科研需求，智元将投入千台具身智能设备，双方将进行课程共建、课题共研、实训共育，打通产业前沿技术与高校人才培养的衔接壁垒。首批合作的 20 多所高等院校包括北京大学、清华大学、浙江大学、华南理工大学、上海交通大学、西安交通大学、东南大学、中山大学等。智元将投入包括精灵、灵犀、远征在内的轮式、半尺寸和全尺寸人形机器人以及酷拓四足机器人，投入机型覆盖了智元全系列本体产品，投入总数超过一千台，解决高校机器短缺的问题。同时，智元还将提供 AIMA 开发平台，为高校系统化教学、学生自主研发提供完整工具支撑。作为智元推出的具身智能全域技术生态底座，AIMA 包含灵心平台 LinkSoul（具身智能体开发应用平台）、灵创平台 LinkCraft（机器人综合智能创作平台）、精灵平台 Genie Studio（一站式全流程具身作业智能平台），为高校学生提供“硬件真机实训 + 软件平台研发”的双轨教学体系。依托全套软件生态，高校学子可系统性学习具身智能软硬件原理、完成模型训练、算法调试、场景开发、任务实现与二次开发等，实现从理论学习到真机落地的完整闭环。本次智元提供机器本体与软件会员权益的总额达到 2 亿。智元也将探索建立常态化高校交流机制，支持优质项目落地，逐步形成可持续、可复制的具身智能校企合作模式。据IT之家此前报道，在 2026 APC 智元合作伙伴大会上，智元推出“元苼生态发展计划”，未来五年将投入超过 20 亿元专项资金，用于科研学术创新、教育人才培养、生态伙伴发展以及开发社区运营。目前，“元苼生态发展计划”已经建联国内外 237 所科研院校，合作了 500+ 家生态合作伙伴，累积了 10000+ 应用开发者和 70000+ 订阅开发者。据财经杂志 10 月 13 日报道，智元创新近期启动了新一轮融资，融资额约 10 亿元 —15 亿元，本轮融资已接近收尾，最新估值约 500 亿元。智元是一家以具身智能为核心技术方向的通用 AI 机器人公司，于 2023 年成立。9 月 24 日，智元第 2 万台具身智能机器人宣布下线，刷新全球量产纪录。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，科技媒体 ximitime 昨日（10 月 15 日）发布博文，通过挖掘 Mi Code 代码，发现了 REDMI Turbo 6 及 REDMI Turbo 6 Max 两款手机的踪迹。从已曝光的型号看，小米或将继续采用“同一硬件、不同品牌命名”的策略：中国市场的 REDMI Turbo 6 / Turbo 6 Max，预计在海外以 POCO X9 Pro / X9 Pro Max 的名义销售，而印度市场则可能同时出现 REDMI Turbo 与 POCO 两个系列。在 REDMI Turbo 6 方面，在海外市场名为 POCO X9 Pro，内部代号为 sofia，也称为 Q10，目前已发现 2703BPC40G、2703BRT40I、2703BPC40I、M407CF 四款型号。在 REDMI Turbo 6 Max 方面，该机在海外市场预估名为 POCO X9 Pro Max，内部代号“denver”，也称为 Q10U，目前已发现 27011RT78I、27011PC78I 和 27011PC78G 三款型号。上市时间方面，爆料根据型号命名规律推测，新机最快可能在 2027 年 1 月至 3 月之间发布。IT之家曾于今年 7 月发布博文，分享了一张小米 REDMI Turbo 6 Max 手机的渲染图。规格方面，该机最大的亮点在于配备 10000mAh 容量电池，以及 7 英寸屏幕，处理器可能使用联发科天玑 9500s 或者天玑 9600s。小米 REDMI Turbo 5 系列手机发布于 1 月 29 日，分为标准版和 Max 机型。其中 REDMI Turbo 5 手机搭载天玑 8500-Ultra 处理器，REDMI Turbo 5 Max 手机则首发天玑 9500s 处理器：REDMI Turbo 5：原价 2299 元、首销 1999 元起；REDMI Turbo 5 Max：原价 2499 元、首销 2199 元起。▲ IT之家开箱：小米 REDMI Turbo 5 Max 手机图赏

articles.title: 腾讯 WorkBuddy 和 CodeBuddy 宣布 DeepSeek 服务故障用户 7 天内积分全额返还，额外送 500 积分
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，DeepSeek 网页 / API 服务 10 月 15 日早间出现服务问题，经过近 5 个小时的修复恢复正常。对此，DeepSeek 官方开放平台宣布补偿所有 API 用户 7 天内的消耗金额。腾讯 WorkBuddy 和 CodeBuddy 今日跟进发布补偿公告，针对在 WorkBuddy 或 CodeBuddy 国内版端内使用 DeepSeek 模型并受到影响的用户，其在 10 月 8 日 ~14 日期间使用 DeepSeek 模型所消耗的积分将给予全额返还，7 个工作日内到账。同时，考虑到此次事件对用户造成体验不佳影响，WorkBuddy 和 CodeBuddy 宣布面向国内版全量用户额外赠送 500 积分，均可在 10 月 22 日 24 点前进入“用量管理”页面手动领取，积分有效期为一个月。IT之家注意到，这是 DeepSeek 本月以来遇到的最大规模服务问题，网友 10 月 15 日早间在 DeepSeek 中对话提示“服务器暂时不可用”；WorkBuddy 也提示“DeepSeek 原厂故障中”，建议切换至其他模型。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据易车消息，东风风神 L8+ 将于 10 月 23 日正式上市。新车搭载天元智驾 T800，采用 Momenta R7 世界模型，配备英伟达 Thor-U 芯片，算力可达 700TOPS，支持城市和高速 NOA。动力方面，东风风神 L8+ 搭载 1.5T 发动机 + 电机组成的插电混动系统。据IT之家此前报道，东风风神在今年 7 月宣布，下半年将发布风神 L8Y/L8+/L9/E80 四款新车。其中风神 L8+ 剑指“同级最强智能辅助驾驶产品”，宣称刷新同级车型的智能体验上限。内饰方面，风神 L8+ 搭载内嵌式液晶仪表以及大尺寸悬浮中控屏，并配备了三辐式多功能方向盘。此外，新车还配备了内饰氛围灯、手机无线充电、全景天窗、19 扬声器 WANOS 全景声音响、娱乐吸顶屏、后排小桌板等配置。

articles.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. articles.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Yet benchmark items produce far more information than the scores we typically extract from them: a full transcript of how each model solved the task. We investigate whether these transcripts can be used to assess model capabilities even after benchmark scores have saturated. We simulate saturation retrospectively using historical benchmark and model releases, and test whether protocols that access only correctly solved transcripts from saturated benchmarks can predict capabilities measured on held-out, unsaturated items. articles.title: Value-Informed Schedule Trimming for Accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo Guidance in Discrete Diffusion
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Active guidance steps require additional reward evaluations and, for gradient-based proposals, value-gradient computations. Sparse guidance reduces this cost by guiding only a subset of timesteps, but commonly used schedules are fixed heuristics whose effectiveness can vary substantially across tasks. We propose VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects guided timesteps under a fixed budget. VISTA formulates sparse guidance as approximation of the ideal full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable upper bound on \(\ell_1\) path deviation. articles.title: AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20675v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents pair reasoning models with harnesses that organize model calls, execute tools, load skill instructions, and retain history in memory. Understanding agent performance requires linking execution conditions to outcomes, behavior, and resource use. We introduce AlphaDiana, a measurement system with modular interfaces for datasets, agents, environments, and scorers. It preserves harness-native control loops while controlling file reuse and memory retention separately. AlphaDiana supports macro analyses of complete agents and micro interventions on agent components such as tools, skills, and memory under matched conditions. We study three open-source models and three open-source harnesses on five answer-based benchmarks, with two models also tested on two interactive benchmarks. articles.title: When Correctness Feedback Erases Evidence: Phase-Separated Completeness Auditing in Verus
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20676v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Correctness feedback suppresses the very evidence that specification-completeness auditing is designed to uncover: programs that satisfy a written contract but violate intended behavior. We demonstrate this objective reversal on 12 Verus/Rust tasks across four model families under matched call budgets. Independent no-feedback discovery more than doubles certified-witness yield relative to IntentShield's corrective-feedback loop (59.0% versus 27.1%). A format-matched iterative control places the larger share of this gap in feedback content, not independent restarts. The advantage holds in every model family and survives parser repair. A separate phase-separated execution matches the aggregate yield without reusing responses; most certified witnesses also fail held-out cases. articles.title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. We introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for selective VLM safety. CNRF constructs context-matched benign-harmful counterfactual pairs, uses their representation differences as capability-related risk directions, and estimates neighborhood support separately from risk. This separation prevents unfamiliarity from being conflated with harmfulness and enables selective intervention rather than blanket rejection. A victim-adaptive interface accommodates different safety observations across VLM architectures and routes selected requests for same-victim response review, which either releases acceptable candidates or produces constrained alternatives with reduced harmful capability

articles.title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. We introduce IneqAgent, an agentic framework combining LLM reasoning with symbolic computation for inequality proving in Lean4. Lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search coordinates lemma construction, goal reformulation, and symbolic backend selection. Complementary sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution backends produce exact certificates for local Lean proof generation. The agent integrates these proofs with LLM-generated steps and uses Lean feedback to construct complete proofs checked against the original theorem statements. On four benchmarks, IneqAgent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash solves 175 of 186 problems (94.09%), achieving the highest overall success rate among the evaluated methods. Across four backbones, it achieves higher success rates at low LLM inference cost

articles.title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. An analyst then uses verifier feedback and diagnostic tools to propose revisions, which a generator converts into refined expressions. articles.title: When Reality Outpaces Cognition: A New Scaling Principle for Reliable Intelligence
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? We formulate this as a theory- and model-agnostic challenge in which systems must infer reliable actions for increasingly distant future states across a growing observation--reality gap. We operationalize this challenge through the effective Speed of Coherent Cognition (\(S_C^{\mathrm{eff}}\)), defined as the highest tested Speed of Reality (\(S_R\)) through which a system continuously satisfies a predefined behavioural reliability criterion from baseline. As a proof of concept, reinforcement-learning agents are trained at the baseline \(S_R\) and evaluated, without retraining, as \(S_R\) is increased by up to \(50\times\) while computational resources remain fixed. articles.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20780v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions. Our key intuition is to turn execution-verified repairs into reusable supervision, moving repair search into data construction and training so that a learned model can intervene at runtime without repeatedly testing alternatives. articles.title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. articles.title: EvolvingBrain: An Adaptive Skill System for Multi-modal Agents Self-Evolution in Open Worlds
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-modal agents have made significant progress in interacting with open worlds. However, their ability to self-evolve remains limited. Supervised fine-tuning enables imitation but not active experience organization, while outcome-based reinforcement learning promotes exploration yet underuses intermediate trajectory information. Therefore, we propose EvolvingBrain, which uses an adaptive skill system as the brain for agent self-evolution, consisting of two following components. Stratified Skill Self-Evolution: extracts Procedural Patterns and Problematic Patterns from model-specific trajectories, summarizes experience by generating skills, and evolves through multiple interactions with the open world, ultimately forming a Stratified Skill Architecture consisting of Domain, Plan, and Action/Trap Skills, which provides the agent with a multi-granularity knowledge repository and a novel evolution approach. articles.title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Yet continuation repeats the stale conclusion in most conflicts, and the separate call follows the current evidence far more often. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A self-improving agent has to decide which new skills to keep, and in practice it keeps whatever earns a high reward, convinces a judge model, or compresses its library, even when the skill is wrong. That is fine until the answers have to be exactly right: over a table of transactions, a total is either right or wrong. We ask a harder question: can an agent grow what it can compute with no reward, no judge, and no answer key, and still be exactly right? A single frozen model runs two nested loops over a small, exact domain-specific language (DSL). The inner loop answers new questions only when two independently written expressions agree on every record. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20822v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. articles.title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20836v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. We formulate this choice as a compute-aware three-action controller, scoring terminal actions by predicted answer success and expansion by a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate, with compute cost priced explicitly. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. On held-out width expansion and revision tasks, the controller improves observed utility over calibration-selected fixed policies while reducing normalized online compute by about 30% and 16%, respectively. articles.title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20845v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Skill-policy co-evolution, in which an agent's policy model and its skill bank improve each other during training, is a promising paradigm for self-improving agents. Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. In this paper, we first establish, through theoretical and empirical analysis, that the fragility hidden by this blind spot is not incidental. articles.title: Anticipatory Commonsense with Moving Objects: An ASP-Based Framework for Predictive Reasoning with Interacting Trajectories
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a general declarative framework for anticipatory reasoning about interactive motion in complex dynamic environments. Our focus is on (explainable) anticipatory space-time mental model formation at a semantic level to heuristically guide low-level motion computation. Our method is hybrid, modular and elaboration tolerant integrating: 1) An ASP model characterising the dynamics of interactive motion trajectories; 2) Semantically-guided prediction for deriving `branching trajectory futures'; and 3) An energy-based {optimisation} model to evaluate, rank and filter anticipations. We evaluate with the Argoverse 2 benchmark, where each anticipated trajectory carries an explicit, inspectable event-level hypothesis, unlike end-to-end stochastic prediction.

articles.title: A Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM): Proportionate Access and Capability Limits for Comprehensive Frontier AI Safety
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. That framing runs together two separate decisions. One is how capable a system may become. The other is who may obtain a given capability, and on what terms. This paper is about the second decision. We propose a Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM) that sorts access by purpose, safety, and capability instead of by release artifact. Tier 1, AI for Learning, is broadly accessible and deliberately capability-bounded. Tier 2, AI for Exploration, serves research and development under registration, identity, and usage controls that tighten as capability rises. Tier 3, Full-Scale Frontier AI, is available only through structured, recorded, and accountable access. articles.title: Defining and Generating Compositional Structure
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20922v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20636v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sampling from continuous flow-based generators such as flow matching models requires numerical ODE or SDE integration, making inference cost depend on the number of function evaluations (NFEs). In practice, the sampling budget is inherited from prior work or selected through expensive FID-versus-NFE sweeps, using FID to assess image-generation quality, requiring sample generation and evaluation at multiple budgets. This makes sampling-budget selection dependent on repeated empirical evaluation. articles.content:

Abstract: Research on deceptive alignment is becoming increasingly urgent as frontier-model capabilities advance and their risk of causing catastrophic harm increases. Alignment faking is a form of deceptive alignment, with the compliance gap serving as a key behavioural indicator. This behaviour remains understudied in small LLMs and prior mechanistic interventions have not been shown to mitigate the compliance gap. We test whether steering SAE (sparse autoencoders) features associated with deontological ethics can mitigate this behaviour. We use a novel bag-of-words feature elicitation pipeline for SAE steering to identify what we construe as concept-level steering directions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is credited with gains beyond the domain its rewards check, such as higher MMLU accuracy after training on mathematics. Such accuracies are usually read out of the model's text by an answer extractor. A model that learns to write its answer where the extractor looks can therefore score higher without answering better. We measure how much of the gain reported by extractors copied from public code arises this way. We generate outputs from a base model and its RL model and score them twice: with those extractors, and with one extractor of our own that reads a stated answer whether it is in the answer box \boxed{} or in the text. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Global streamflow forecasting supports flood preparedness, yet data-driven models trained on reanalysis lose skill when driven by operational forecasts, increasingly so with lead time. AIFL addresses this shift with a two-stage transfer-learning recipe and a deterministic LSTM, but it feeds one forecast lead time into the whole input window and gives no uncertainty. We ask how far this open recipe can be extended without changing its recurrent core. KNOU-Flood keeps a single-layer LSTM and the two-stage training and changes the information around it: a longer input window (424 days), lead-aware forecast inputs, GraphCast as a second forecast source next to ECMWF HRES, and a latent-noise ensemble trained with the fair CRPS. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20680v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary. We study how much activation data SAEs need by training four SAE architectures on three language models with budgets ranging from 5M tokens to a 500M-token reference. We measure two notions of convergence: functional behavior on standard evaluations and one-to-one reproducibility of learned features. Functional data requirements are strongly metric-dependent: reconstruction often approaches the full-data reference at substantially smaller budgets, whereas feature reproducibility continues to improve with data. articles.content:

Abstract: We introduce TurboMamba, a language-model architecture for faster inference, faster training, and better token prediction. A global Mamba-3 model runs once per completed token block. A small Transformer uses this global context and earlier tokens within the block to predict the next token. Three lightweight additions improve local predictions: direct access to the previous block's last token, a small correction to next-token scores, and a learned mixture with recent-token frequencies. We compare twelve small-scale implementations on public FineWeb-Edu, with comparable parameter counts and shared training-budget caps. The baselines include Transformer, Mamba-3, Jamba, and Zamba. The Jamba and Zamba versions use Mamba-3 in place of their original Mamba modules. TurboMamba achieves the lowest mean test prediction loss (negative log-likelihood, NLL) among all twelve models. Abstract: Code models write Python when the prompt does not say which language to use. We propose a topology-aware representation learning framework that integrates persistent homology into a DMAE backbone to explicitly encode global structural connectivity. A persistence-guided masking strategy prioritizes patches associated with persistent topological features, while an auxiliary persistent-homology decoder encourages the latent representation to retain information about topological feature counts across connected components, tunnels, and voids. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. articles.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. articles.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We find that residual control throughout the denoising network yields the most consistent improvements. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. Abstract: Many modern learning problems require comparing probability distributions whose individual observations are themselves probability measures, naturally giving rise to meta-measures in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(\Omega))$. articles.content:

Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to uncover how neural networks use their parameters to implement their impressive neural algorithms. Although previous work has uncovered substantial structure in the intermediate representations that networks use, little progress has been made to understand how the parameters and nonlinearities of networks perform computations on those representations. In this work, we present a method that brings us closer to this understanding by decomposing a language model's parameters into subcomponents that each implement only a small part of the model's learned algorithm, while simultaneously requiring only a small fraction of those subcomponents to account for the network's behavior on any input. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) trained on vast amounts of data have demonstrated impressive performance over a range of tasks, but future performance gains will require increasing amounts of data and compute. Federated Learning (FL) facilitates training on decentralized private data, but client resource limitations can make training impractical, particularly as model sizes continue to expand. These resource constraints make the assumption of a shared server-client architecture impractical. Model heterogeneous FL offers a promising alternative by adapting model size to client capabilities; however, previous work is limited to the pre-training setting, and conclusions on sub-network selection do not necessarily hold for fine-tuning. Abstract: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces. Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder. An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. articles.content:

Abstract: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. The post-training method for such generators remains a limitation: a corpus lists the graphs that solved a query but never ranks them, leaving continued supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with no per-query preference to exploit. Without such a preference, the generator drifts toward the topologies the corpus contains most often rather than those that suit each query, so a gain on one task can come at a cost on another. articles.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Always-on virtual assistants increasingly personalize on-device to new user-specific commands via few-shot fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), but this adaptation is evaluated almost exclusively on whether it learns the new commands, not on whether the assistant can still recognize an input that matches none of its intents - the out-of-scope (OOS) rejection problem. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20763v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. Abstract: Automating organizational work means answering many small typed questions about one piece of state (does this email need a reply, how urgent is it, who owns it) with probabilities good enough to act on without a human. The open typed-decision model we compare against, like a standard cross-encoder, answers each question with a separate pass over the input. Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in social interactions, where appropriate responses require recognizing implicit cues, inferring mental states, identifying conflicts, and considering potential consequences. Abstract: Recent literature shows that unsafe tool calls can often accompany textual refusals in language models. Notably, using behavioral labels from an NF4 copy enables stable intervention estimation even with very few scenarios. Furthermore, these alignment improvements transfer effectively across languages: five-language NF4-supervised directions successfully transfer to held-out Arabic, reducing unsafe violations in Llama-3.1-8B by 21.95 percentage points without target-language tuning. articles.title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20824v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. After presenting the pipeline and data, extensive experiments on 63~public and in-house tasks show good performance on Wolof understanding and generation while remaining effective on other languages and cross-lingual skills, with the 8B and 14B models being particularly competitive with substantially larger commercial systems. The models are currently being evaluated in internal customer-care pilots and are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Orange/wolof-lm .

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20828v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Reverse CoT generation (RCG) is cheaper because it conditions on the known answer, but access to this answer can lead to post-hoc rationalization and a mismatch with the student's answer-free inference setting. We propose CoTranslator, which learns to translate reverse CoT responses toward the distribution of verified forward responses. Trained on a small set of paired reverse and rejection-sampled forward responses, it supports large-scale generation and verification of student training data. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). Abstract: Typology-aware tokenizers are motivated by the claim that segmentation which respects morpheme boundaries preserves information that frequency-driven segmentation destroys. Studies routinely establish that it helps while assuming the boundaries must be linguistically correct. We separate them. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on context compaction: when the interaction history outgrows the context window, a compressor replaces it with a natural-language summary. We show that these summaries contain more than a record of what happened. Compaction prompts ask for decisions and next steps, so each summary mixes facts established by the environment with reasoning written by the compressor, and the agent cannot tell the two apart afterwards. In an analysis of a widely used structured compressor, 83% of failed runs trace back to an action that carries out a specific summary entry, most of which no environment output supports. We propose Source-Judged Compaction (SJC), a training-free post-processing step that scores each summary entry for whether it has a source in the environment outputs or the previous summary, and removes the entries that do not. articles.title: BD-HazardVLM: Probing Vision-Language Models for Latent Defensive-Driving Hazards in Bangladesh Road Scenes
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used for driving-scene understanding, yet their defensive reasoning under weakly structured Global South traffic remains unclear. We introduce BD-HazardVLM, a diagnostic benchmark of 500 Bangladesh road-scene images, comprising 375 from RSUD20K and 125 from TFP-BD, annotated for hazard presence, primary hazard category, risk timing, severity, defensive actions, visible evidence, and hallucination- and Western-road-bias traps. We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and MiniCPM-V-4.6 using a shared zero-shot task definition and structured output schema. Binary hazard-presence accuracy ranges from 88.0 percent to 89.2 percent, essentially matching the 89.0 percent majority-class baseline. Fine-grained reasoning is substantially weaker: category accuracy remains below 40 percent, risk-timing accuracy ranges from 1.6 percent to 12.4 percent, and exact defensive-action matching remains below 2 percent.

Abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Abstract: Representation alignment improves and accelerates diffusion training by encouraging intermediate features to match a pretrained visual encoder. LAP modifies only the alignment target, and requires no changes to diffusion training or inference. articles.content:

Abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. Abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. Abstract: Negation is a fundamental aspect of language understanding and it is important vision-language models (VLMs) are able to process it effectively. While layerwise analysis shows that PaliGemma2-3B shifts object attention to the alternative under negation, our headwise ablations suggest this is a byproduct rather than a negation processing mechanism. articles.title: DefoliationCAM: An Edge-AI System for Real-Time Insect Defoliation Severity Assessment in Grapevines
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20879v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Insect-induced defoliation threatens grapevine health and yield, yet severity assessment relies on subjective manual scouting. We developed DefoliationCAM (D-CAM), a solar-powered edge AI system that estimates canopy defoliation and transmits results via LoRa to a web dashboard. The pipeline uses YOLOX-Nano to localize grapevine cordons in 4K images and a MobileNet-based classifier with lightweight channel attention to classify 320 x 320 pixel patches. Abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. arXiv:2610.20917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. Common pruning proxies, such as opacity, activation frequency, or parameter magnitude, do not measure whether removing a row changes the model's voxel decisions. We introduce Decision-FLIP, a budget-free compilation framework whose scoring and structure selection need only unlabeled calibration inputs. Exact Mean-FLIP scores each persistent row by the number of voxel argmax decisions that change when the row is removed from the readout; a guarded Otsu split of the log-score distribution selects the survivor count without a target and abstains when the split is unsupported; and the survivors are physically compiled into a smaller checkpoint, so camera sampling, attention, and aggregation shrink with the bank. articles.title: VELD-QA: A Large-Scale Dataset for Visual Evidence Grounding and Question Answering in Long Documents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. We present VELD-QA, a large-scale benchmark for Visual Evidence grounding and question answering in Long Documents. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. We evaluate nine vision-language models under four evidence settings and seven retrieval-augmented and agentic systems. Our analysis identifies bottlenecks in evidence localization and interpretation. Retrieval-based methods substantially underperform the oracle setting with ground-truth supporting pages

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geo-foundation models (GFMs) are typically evaluated by downstream task predictive performance, revealing little about which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. This limits developers' ability to test hypotheses about model behaviour and users' ability to select models for new tasks. We propose Physics-Informed Concept Probing (PiCo), a post-hoc framework for explaining GFM predictions. PiCo identifies concept vectors in a GFM's embedding space by generating synthetic multispectral satellite observations from a 3D radiative transfer model coupled with a game engine. These vectors reveal physical sensitivities that inform domain-based hypotheses about downstream performance. arXiv:2610.20990v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Current approaches focus on distilling the number of diffusion steps, neglecting potential redundancies of the training data. In this paper, we explore the potential of harnessing eigensamples to train diffusion models on significantly smaller datasets, while preserving model performance. To mitigate the sensitivity to affine transformations of eigenimages, we harness the latent space of a pre-trained CLIP model. We next compute latent eigenvectors by performing principal component analysis (PCA) in CLIP space. Abstract: Data selection reallocates training support across visual concepts, including objects, attributes, color, texture, and backgrounds. Different allocation strategies may produce varied downstream model behavior, especially for tail concepts supported by only a few samples. Discarding them can hurt test-time robustness, while overemphasizing samples lying on category boundaries may introduce unstable training signals. This work explicitly investigates this relationship across fine-grained, spurious-correlation, and general image classification, as well as multimodal pretraining. Specifically, we use sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to extract concept activations from individual images. During selection, we accumulate the dataset-level concept support for each added sample. Abstract: Identifying individual dogs from barks in real-world videos remains challenging and largely unexplored. Solving this problem would enable long-term behavioral analysis, veterinary monitoring, and animal welfare monitoring by attributing vocalizations and behaviors to the correct individual. Real-world videos are challenging because multiple dogs may bark simultaneously, become occluded, or move in and out of view. Prior studies show that canine vocalizations and visual appearance contain discriminative identity information, but these modalities have largely been studied independently. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are a promising approach to general purpose robot manipulation. While the internal computation of vision-language models, which compose the backbone of VLAs, has been studied extensively, less is known about how their perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into action in VLA models. We study this question mechanistically in three frontier VLA models ($\pi_{0.5}$, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) by analyzing the causal pathways through which the input image and the instruction shape actions. Across the three models, activation patching shows that causally relevant information influences the action expert (AE) through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, which we term the action-conditioning interface. Abstract: Can better feature discovery improve control over robot behavior through internal interventions and training data? We investigate whether recovering this structure provides an interpretable interface for steering vision-language-action models and shaping the data from which they learn. We show that BSFs recover several multi-dimensional task-relevant features underlying the model's computation (e.g., perception, language, proprioceptive state, episode phase, and control variables). Abstract: Reliable absolute heading estimation is critical for road-vehicle navigation, particularly when magnetic, inertial, or GNSS-based references are degraded. This paper presents a skylight polarization navigation method that estimates vehicle heading by globally optimizing a Rayleigh sky model against measurements from a division-of-focal-plane polarimetric camera. The proposed framework combines a pinhole camera model, a single-scattering Rayleigh polarization model, and a solar position algorithm to synthesize the expected full image angle of polarization distribution for candidate vehicle states. Abstract: A mesh of interceptors defending a fixed site must spread over the predicted arrival point of an approaching object. This is a recurring task in multi-agent robotics: N agents, each covering a disc of radius r, spread over a probability density so that a point drawn from it falls within some agent's disc. We give closed forms for the quantities that bound performance before any policy is chosen, and validate each by Monte Carlo. Abstract: Damage-recovery algorithms often rank gaits from short trials, yet a gait that performs well briefly may not remain effective during continued execution. In reset-free recovery, each trial also changes the physical state inherited by the next. We introduce persistent profile-guided reset-free recovery (PGRR), which predicts multiple outcomes over repeated gait execution and uses conservative uncertainty-aware estimates to guide short online probes without resetting the robot. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20840v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robotic manipulation is inherently geometric, but what shape does the world take inside the policy that performs it? Prior work on vision-language-action (VLA) policies establishes that task-relevant variables are linearly readable from activations, yet readability certifies only that a variable is present and says nothing about the shape its values trace, which may be curved and multi-dimensional. Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, we build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA models. We find that realized geometry is predominantly multi-dimensional and is shaped by the constraints under which the policy acts. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential for mission planning. Abstract: Vehicles that lose control at the handling limit through icing, hydroplaning, or an abrupt evasive maneuver fall outside the operating envelope of production safety systems such as electronic stability control, which focus on preventing instability rather than recovering from it. Expert drivers regain authority in these conditions by drifting. Existing autonomous recovery approaches are validated on idealized scenarios, define "recovered" states empirically and inconsistently, or rely on offline-planned trajectories rather than acting online. We address these gaps by first training a racing policy with reinforcement learning that learns drifting as a time-optimal maneuver, then adapting it to recovery through continued training with a minimum-time reward. arXiv:2610.20875v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. However, effective autonomy requires the robots to make decisions as to how to allocate this energy to maximize information quality over time. In this paper, we study a persistent (infinite-horizon) speed trajectory optimization problem that is posed as a periodic optimal control problem in which a robot repeatedly traverses a fixed closed path, coupling a super-linear propulsion cost with dynamic information gain and decay. Using the information-theoretic quantity of clarity as an information metric, we first derive the necessary conditions for optimal control. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20895v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Satisfying safety constraints for systems with second-order dynamics is challenging because a position constraint may require infeasible deceleration. Higher-order control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an approach for expressing safety conditions for such systems but feasibility depends on the system dynamics and available control authority. We develop a constructive approach for designing feasible safety constraints for second-order control-affine systems. Starting from a signed distance function (SDF), we construct collision-free spheres, i.e., bubbles, in position space, and use their quadratic geometry and overlap to construct a velocity-dependent safety constraint. The associated safe set is represented as a union of intersections and enforced through a quadratic-program safety filter. Abstract: Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) has emerged as an important skill for purposeful robotic manipulation. Given the task of using a knife to "slice bread," a robot must choose to grasp from the handle, whereas for "hand[ing] the knife over," it is preferable for the handle to remain unobstructed for safe handoff. Current approaches for TOG either focus on 2D planar grasping, remain limited by their reliance on task-agnostic grasp generators, or are constrained by reliance on finite, manually-annotated, task-specific grasp datasets that cannot cover all possible grasp-task pairs. To that end, we present TGrasp6D, a vision-language based approach for generating task-oriented 6DoF grasps in a zero-shot manner. Abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Abstract: Generating dynamically feasible motions for legged and manipulating robots requires solving a large, nonlinear, non-convex optimal control problem (OCP) in which contact wrenches must satisfy friction-cone constraints throughout the motion, not only at isolated instants. Existing solvers are sensitive to the initial guess and scale poorly with the number of joints. This paper introduces LEAP, which transcribes the OCP with pseudospectral collocation and, instead of a Newton or SQP solve, integrates a primal--dual gradient flow of a Powell--Hestenes--Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian to compute a solution. Because the flow is stiff, this paper designs a linearly implicit integrator with a Gauss--Newton metric, momentum, and a merit-based step controller that keeps the augmented Lagrangian monotone. Abstract: Executing heavy-duty physical manipulation in unpredictable environments remains a major challenge for quadrupedal robots lacking dedicated manipulators. This paper presents SOMA, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for whole-body non-prehensile manipulation of multi-object stacks using a quadruped robot. articles.title: When a robot can trust reversing wind to find an odour source
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A wind-derived heading can guide a robot towards an odour source even after the wind reverses, but its reliability depends on the plume's transport history. On a quadruped initially facing the source, holding the initial heading reached it in every reversing-wind trial, whereas comparison controllers never settled there. An exact geometric condition links heading correctness to net odour transport, and simulations separate sensing error from departures from nominal flow. Where the alternating wind directions are too close for reversal alone to produce wrong-side headings, the wrong-side rate rises from 1.0% under uniform transport to 4.7% in a stochastic flow. Re-acquiring headings from new odour contact improves simulated search when contact is intermittent. These results identify distinct requirements for wind-guided search: a heading supported by the transport geometry and sufficient intermittent contact to replace it.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Passive human videos of everyday activity offer robots access to a massive amount of human experience without requiring a demonstration for each task. However, using this experience requires recovering knowledge from unstructured video recordings and adapting it to a different body (i.e., the robot). To overcome these challenges, we present mobile code-as-policy (MoCaP), an agentic framework that turns passive human video recordings into guidance for an end-to-end mobile manipulation policy. MoCaP extracts spatial memory and cues of how people prepare to interact with objects, which inform navigation and the search for a manipulation-ready configuration. Guided by passive human experience and current observations, MoCaP uses a closed-loop code-as-policy to coordinate planning and tool use primitives to solve motions under the robot's geometry and kinematic constraints. articles.title: Slip-Induced Fall Suppression During Cornering for a Remotely Operated Motorcycle with a Rear-Wheel-Swing Mechanism
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.21089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slip-induced falls when riding motorcycles are difficult to avoid even for expert riders and represent a major cause of single-vehicle accidents. Despite their prevalence, no practical solution has yet been proposed to suppress this phenomenon. We previously introduced a motorcycle model applicable to systems with both front- and rear- wheel steering. In this paper, we extend that model and formulate the suppression of slip-induced falls as an optimization problem that distributes assistive control inputs according to vehicle speed and road surface conditions. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a remotely operated motorcycle and conducted experiments under two scenarios: slalom driving on a low-friction surface at 5.5 m/s, and turning maneuvers on synthetic ice to simulate driving over manholes on rainy days. The results demonstrate that our approach successfully suppresses falls under these challenging conditions.

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

articles.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
articles.content: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.content: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.content: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

articles.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
articles.content: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.
